key_insight: Large language models can programmatically generate human‑readable code that encodes general design rules, enabling the automatic creation of entire families of quantum experiments that are interpretable and scalable.
problem_solved: Designing novel quantum experiments is combinatorially complex, expert‑dependent, and slow to scale; this work automates and generalizes experiment design by extracting reusable rules via language models.
method: Use language models to write human‑readable code/programs that encode experiment design rules rather than single instances.
Generate families of quantum experiment candidates from the synthesized code and validate them via simulation or lab checks.
Leverage the code’s interpretability for rule extraction, scaling to many variants, and accelerating discovery cycles.
impact: Enables AI‑assisted, scalable discovery in quantum optics/experiments by turning black‑box suggestions into readable, reusable design programs—reducing expert bottlenecks and speeding up iteration. Practitioners gain a pathway to automate experiment generation while preserving interpretability and transferability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM prompt → generated code (human‑readable) → family of experiment schematics → simulation/validation
Side‑by‑side example: short generated code snippet vs. rendered optical circuit/experiment it produces
Bar/line chart: number of novel valid designs discovered vs. baseline/manual design over time
Icon grid highlighting benefits: interpretability, scalability, automation, accelerated discovery
paper_title: Meta-designing quantum experiments with language models
paper_authors: Sören Arlt, Haonan Duan, Felix Li, Sang Michael Xie, Yuhuai Wu
